newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS-Swiss shares rally on, party may not be over.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Swiss shares rally on, party may not be over.

text.p: Swiss shares surged to new records on Friday, helped by a rally in bonds and the strong dollar, with analysts saying there may be room for even more gains ahead.
The 19-share blue chip Swiss Market Index surged to its seventh closing high in a row Friday, rising 48.1 points, or over to end at 4,357.9 points.

The latest gains left bourse traders trying to recall when, if ever, the SMI had set seven straight closing highs. At the same time, Swiss bond yields are now seen at levels comparable to lows last set in late 1979.
Traders said Swiss share markets were helped by recent upgrades by bank analysts and brokers.
"We just have increased our price target to 2,900 from 2,800 by end-1997 for the Swiss Performance Index," said Hans Kaufmann at Bank Julius Baer.
The broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) also hit a new high on Friday of 2,783.59 points. It has risen from levels of roughly 2,500 at the start of the year.
At Lehman Brothers, London-based analyst Ian Scott said his firm raised its weighting for Switzerland earlier this week.
"We raised ours on Monday from an underweight position to an overweight position. We had been underweight since October 1995," he said.
He said that a recent decline in the Swiss franc had contributed to a better earnings outlook for Swiss companies.
He said that the Swiss market should also offer something of a safe haven, given that Lehman is anticipating a mild correction in equity markets generally.

Swiss stocks already hit new highs on Friday before release of U.S. employment data for January. The latest data, which showed no real threat of inflation from earnings, touched off gains in world bond markets and added to the positive sentiment.
The average yield of Swiss Federal bonds, which is calculated at midday, was at 3.62 percent on Friday.

It had been slightly lower once or twice in the past two years. But analysts say the basket of bonds which comprise the index is rebalanced at the start of the year, which effectively raises the yield early in the year.
Kaufmann said there were many reasons for the latest rally.
Alongside recent increased weightings by several U.S. brokers, the Swiss National Bank also appears determined to keep interest rates low.
Swiss mortgage rates have also lately started to decline.

Swiss companies are likely to profit significantly from the Swiss franc's deprecation -- which has not only been against the dollar but also against European currencies -- because it should spur exports. Analysts were likely to take account of this in their forecasts for Swiss companies in the first quarter.
"I am convinced you will see upwards (earnings) revisions going on, especially in late spring," Kaufmann said.
Swiss banks have also been strong lately. Heavy volume on Swiss exchanges was also likely to boost commission income.
At Credit Suisse First Boston, technical analysts believe the market also has more room to the upside.
"We think that for the moment, the move to the upside is not over yet," said Beat Grunder, technical analyst at CSFB.
Grunder saw significant resistance is at 4,360.
But beyond that, he said the SMI may have room to get to 4,550 before the end of the 1997.
Few traders see few signs the market has overheated given what appears to be an insatiable need by investors for a place to put liquidity.

"There is certainly an investment need. There is a lot of money in the financial market," said another Swiss share analyst. "Everyone is cautious, and there may be overheating but only in a few shares," he added.
As long as the SNB saw no need to raise interest rates, the rally could continue. "An interest rate rise would be poisonous for shares," he said. -- Zurich Editorial, +41 1 631 7340
